chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from his men, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, for Allah there are two cities, one of them in the east and the other in the west. Upon them is a wall of iron, and upon each one of them are a thousand thousand gates. In them are seventy thousand thousand languages; each language is spoken differently from the language of its companion. And I know all the languages, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and there is no hujjah over them other than me and al-Husayn, my brother.”

key_terms.أَعْرِفُ: I know fully or recognize comprehensively
key_terms.حُجَّةٌ: Divine proof or authority over creation
key_terms.لُغَةٍ: A language or mode of speech
key_terms.مَدِينَتَيْنِ: Two cities described as belonging to Allah

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about the two cities in the east and west say about the knowledge and authority of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (عليهما السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes two extraordinary cities belonging to Allah, distinguished by immense scale, fortified walls, and countless languages. It emphasizes the unique divine authority and comprehensive knowledge granted to al-Hasan and al-Husayn (عليهما السلام), presenting their status as hujjah over creation.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: 'For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are two cities, one of them in the east and the other one in the west. Upon those there are walls of iron, and upon each one of these there are a thousand (upon) thousand (million) shutters, and therein seventy thousand (upon) thousand (million) languages are spoken, every language being different from its counterpart, and I<sup>asws</sup> understand the entirety of the languages, and whatever there is in them, and what is between them, and there is no Divine Authority upon these two apart from me<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> my<sup>asws</sup> brother<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from ya‘qub ibn Yazid from ibn abu ‘Umayr from his people from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Al-Hassan (a.s.) has said, ‘Allah has two cities. One is in the east and the other is in the west. They have a boundary around them that is made of iron and each one has a million doors. Seven thousand different languages exist therein and know all those languages and all that is therein. There is no one who would possess Leadership with Divine Authority except me and my brother, al-Husayn (a.s.).’
